request.system:
You review answers given by a customer-support assistant for a software product called Relay. You decide whether one answer is good enough to send to a customer. Your verdict is used to compare versions of the assistant, so apply the same standard every time.

The input is JSON with:

- conversation: the customer's messages and the assistant's replies, in order.
- articles: the help-centre articles the assistant found. These are the only source the assistant is allowed to use for how the product works.
- account_facts: what the assistant's tools told it about this customer's own account (setup steps done and missing, edition, seats, health, account owner, renewal). The assistant is allowed to state these.

Judge the assistant's replies on four points:

1. Grounded. Every product step, limit or feature the assistant states can be found in the articles, and every statement about the customer's account can be found in account_facts. Anything else stated as fact is a failure, even if it happens to be true. Offering further help, or naming the account owner as the person to ask about prices, is not a failure.
2. Answers the question. The customer could act on the reply without asking again.
3. Short and clear. The next step or two, in plain words. No long preamble.
4. No promises. No price, discount, date or commitment.

Return:

- verdict: "pass" when all four points hold, otherwise "fail".
- score: 1 to 5. 5 = all four points hold fully. 4 = all hold, with a small weakness in clarity. 3 or lower = at least one point fails.
- reason: one sentence naming the point that decided it.

A clarifying question in reply to a vague message is fine and is not a failure of point 2.

{"conversation": [{"role": "customer", "text": "How do automation rules work with recurring cards?"}, {"role": "agent", "text": "Automation rules work on recurring cards. **Each time a new copy of the card is created, the rule runs on it.**

To set up a rule:
1. Open the board and click the **Automation** button.
2. Choose a trigger, such as "card moves to Done."
3. Add conditions if you want them. They're optional.
4. Add one or more actions, such as "notify the reporter."

You're on the Standard edition, so your workspace can have up to 15 rules. If you reach that limit, your existing rules keep running, but you can't add new ones.

This comes from the help centre article **"Automation rules."**

Your setup still has two steps left: connecting an integration and setting up single sign-on. Tell me if you'd like help with either one."}], "articles": [{"title": "Automation rules", "text": "# Automation rules

An automation rule does something for you when something happens on a board. Example: when a card moves to Done, notify the reporter. Create rules from the Automation button on any board: choose a trigger, optional conditions, and one or more actions.

Rules also work with recurring cards: the rule runs each time a new copy of the card is created.

The number of rules per workspace depends on your edition: 5 on Free, 15 on Standard, 60 on Premium, and no practical limit on Enterprise. When you reach the limit, existing rules keep running but you cannot add new ones.

Search keywords: automate automation rule rules trigger action limit
"}, {"title": "An automation rule did not run, or runs twice", "text": "# An automation rule did not run, or runs twice

If a rule did not run, open the Automation panel on the board and look at the rule's run history. The most common causes are: the rule is switched off; the trigger is on a different list than the one the card moved to; or a condition (label, assignee) did not match.

If a rule sends two notifications for every card, two rules have the same trigger. Check for a copy of the rule on the board and in the workspace template the board was created from. Switch one of them off.
"}, {"title": "Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise", "text": "# Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise

What each edition includes:

- Free: up to 10 users, 5 automation rules, 2 integrations. No single sign-on, no guests, no Relay Assist.
- Standard: 15 automation rules, 3 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 10 Relay Assist credits per seat per month if you add Relay Assist.
- Premium: 60 automation rules, 10 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 40 Assist credits per seat per month.
- Enterprise: no practical limit on rules or integrations, and 150 Assist credits per seat per month.

This article describes features only. For prices, a quote, or to change edition, talk to your account owner: an assistant cannot quote or change prices.

Search keywords: plan plans tier tiers compare comparison difference differences included includes include features premium standard enterprise free what do I get
